question.worked_solution:
Either the positive or negative of the expression inside the absolute value must be equal to the right-hand side of the equation.

So, we set up the two corresponding equations and solve them independently:

- If $|\frac{7}{5}z+3|=\frac{7}{5}z+3,$ we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\frac{7}{5}z+3| & =1 \\ \frac{7}{5}z+3 & =1 \\ \frac{7}{5}z & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying both sides of the equation by $\frac{5}{7}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{7}{5}z & =-2 \\ (\frac{5}{7})\cdot (\frac{7}{5}z) & =(\frac{5}{7})\cdot (-2) \\ (\cancel{\frac{5}{7}})\cdot (\cancel{\frac{7}{5}}z) & =-\frac{10}{7} \\ z & =-\frac{10}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

- If $|\frac{7}{5}z+3|=-(\frac{7}{5}z+3),$ we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\frac{7}{5}z+3| & =1 \\ -(\frac{7}{5}z+3) & =1 \\ -\frac{7}{5}z-3 & =1 \\ -\frac{7}{5}z & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying both sides of the equation by $-\frac{5}{7}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{7}{5}z & =4 \\ (-\frac{5}{7})\cdot (-\frac{7}{5}z) & =(-\frac{5}{7})\cdot (4) \\ (\cancel{-\frac{5}{7}})\cdot (\cancel{-\frac{7}{5}}z) & =-\frac{20}{7} \\ z & =-\frac{20}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $z=-\frac{20}{7}$ and $z=-\frac{10}{7}.$
